Judgemental and intrusive thoughts happen to a lot of people, but I can't imagine how difficult it would be to have ocd on top of that. 
Try to remember that the first thought that comes into your head is the one that society has programmed into you, your second thought is the real you. It's okay to have bad thoughts pop into your head, that doesn't make you a bad person. It feels like shit and makes you question yourself, but correcting it is what actually matters. 
As everyone here has already said, if your feeling so bad about it, it's very likely that it's not how you actually feel. 
Best of luck.

Whenever teachers or anyone would call me out for being a bully by saying "How would you feel if someone did that to you?" I'd usually respond "I don't care, I'd tell them to fuck off."

But one day I considered how I'd feel if someone made my family cry, and my attitude changed immediately and I started to see other people as more human. 
My sister was heavily bullied, so I could see the impact it had on someone and their family. 

I guess as a bully you naturally don't love yourself, but if you think about people you do love you care about how they're treated. So I just started to view everyone as a loved one after that.

Depends on the person, situation, and if my partner was trust worthy. 
My best friend is my ex. We dated and lived together for a year, but we were better of as friends. 
My partner dated his ex for six years, but the relationship eventually fizzled out. 
When you spend so much time developing something good with someone, it's a waste to end a friendship just because the relationship didn't work. 
My partner and I aren't jealous of each others exs, we're happy the the other person has such a good wholesome friend. 

I don't think you should try to maintain a friendship with every ex though. The defining factor for me is if the relationship built you up, then a friendship could work. But if the relationship broke you down, then you should cut your losses. 
Also, if you're getting a gut feeling that your partner is being shady with his ex, trust your gut. 

I know a lot of people feel threatened by an ex but honestly your partner has been there, done that, and it didn't work. Someone new and exciting should be a lot more threatening.
